description_summary: 12-month unduplicated enrollment headcounts broken down by undergraduate or graduate level and race/ethnicity, with separate counts for men, women, and all students. Each record is uniquely identified by IPEDS institution ID (UNITID) and enrollment level (EFFYLEV).

12-month instructional activity totals, measured in credit hours and/or contact hours, for undergraduate and graduate activity; use this table when the question concerns delivered instructional hours or the activity underlying 12-month FTE enrollment rather than student headcount.

Institution-level academic library records for 2015-16, covering library characteristics, collections, expenditures, and services. The survey applies only to degree-granting institutions; expenditure data are available only for institutions with total expenditures over $100,000. Academic Libraries entered IPEDS in 2014-15, so this 2015-16 collection is within the survey’s available period.

Undergraduate admission considerations, applicant counts, admissions, enrolled admitted students, and SAT/ACT test scores for entering first-time, degree/certificate-seeking students. Collected for the Fall 2015 admissions cycle; applies only to institutions without an open-admissions policy for entering first-time students, and test-score data are available only where admission tests are required.

Awards and degrees conferred by six-digit CIP program, award level, first or second major, race/ethnicity, and gender. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, CIPCODE, MAJORNUM, and AWLEVEL, and contains award totals plus sex- and race/ethnicity-specific counts.

Students receiving any degree or certificate, summarized by race/ethnicity and gender. This is one aggregate record per institution, uniquely identified by UNITID, with total, sex-specific, and race/ethnicity-specific student counts.

Students receiving awards broken down by award level, race/ethnicity, gender, and age category. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and AWLEVEL; age groups are under 18, 18–24, 25–39, and 40 or older, but counts are not available for combined race-by-gender-by-age categories.

Programs offered and programs offered via distance education, by CIP program and award level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and CIPCODE: six-digit CIP records show award-level offerings and distance-education offerings, two-digit CIP records summarize the six-digit programs, and CIPCODE 99 provides institution totals; this file measures program offerings rather than awards or students.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFLEVEL and includes total, men’s, and women’s counts overall and by attendance status.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by race/ethnicity, gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFALEVEL and includes total, men’s, and women’s counts for all nine race/ethnicity categories overall and by attendance status.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by distance-education status and student level. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFDELEV and reports total enrollment plus counts exclusively in distance education, in some distance education, or in none; the exclusively-distance-education count is further divided by the student’s location relative to the institution, including same state/jurisdiction, another state/jurisdiction, unknown U.S. state/jurisdiction, and outside the U.S.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by age category, gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID, EFBAGE, and LSTUDY and includes total, men’s, and women’s counts overall and by attendance status. Age enrollment reporting is optional in even-numbered years, so 2015 (odd) has data.

First-time freshman enrollment and recent-high-school-graduate counts broken down by state of residence. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFCSTATE. Residence enrollment reporting is optional in odd-numbered years, so 2015 (odd) has data.

Institution-level measures of total entering class, first-year retention rate, and student-to-faculty ratio, with one record per UNITID. The measures apply only to institutions with undergraduate students; entering-class data are reported only by academic-year institutions, and short-program institutions of less than one year do not have retention data.

Institutional revenues by source, expenditures by category, and assets and liabilities for public institutions using GASB 34/35 accounting standards. Each record is identified by institution (UNITID) and contains the GASB-specific finance measures for fiscal year 2015.

Institutional revenues by source, expenditures by category, and assets and liabilities for private not-for-profit institutions and public institutions using FASB accounting standards. Each record is identified by institution (UNITID) and contains the FASB finance measures for fiscal year 2015.

Institutional revenues by source, expenditures by category, and assets and liabilities for private for-profit institutions using FASB accounting standards. Each record is identified by institution (UNITID); additional revenue-source and expense-function measures introduced beginning with fiscal year 2014 are available in 2015.

Graduation outcomes through 200% of normal time for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates at four-year and less-than-4-year institutions, with completion counts at 100%, 150%, and 200% of normal time. Institution-level records are identified by IPEDS institution ID (UNITID); four-year records concern bachelor’s degree completion, whereas less-than-4-year records concern completion of any degree or certificate.

Graduation and transfer outcomes through 150% of normal time for full-time, first-time undergraduates at four-year and two-year institutions, broken down by gender and race/ethnicity. Rows are uniquely defined by IPEDS institution ID (UNITID), cohort, and cohort graduation status (GRTYPE); four-year data distinguish bachelor’s-seeking and other degree/certificate-seeking cohorts, while two-year data cover the applicable degree-seeking cohort. Counts of completion within 100% of normal time are not available jointly by race/ethnicity and gender for two-year institutions.

Graduation and transfer outcomes through 150% of normal time for the 2012 full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate cohort at less-than-2-year institutions, including enrollment and completion within 100% or 150% of normal time. The records are institution-level, identified by IPEDS institution ID (UNITID), without the gender-by-race/ethnicity breakdown in the companion 150% table.

Staff counts broken down by full- versus part-time status, medical-school status, occupational category, faculty/tenure status, and contract type. Each institution–EAPCAT record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EAPCAT, which defines the occupational category and tenure-status grouping.

Counts of full-time instructional staff broken down by faculty/tenure status, academic rank, race/ethnicity, and gender, with contract type for staff not on the tenure track or in a tenure system. Each institution–SISCAT record is uniquely identified by UNITID and SISCAT, which combines FACSTAT and ARANK; it applies to degree-granting institutions with at least 15 full-time employees and related administrative offices. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting is optional in even-numbered years, so 2015 (odd) has data under the catalog rule.

Full-time new-hire counts broken down by primary occupational category, race/ethnicity, and gender, with instructional new hires additionally classified by faculty/tenure status. Each institution–SNHCAT record is uniquely identified by UNITID and SNHCAT, which defines the primary occupation and instructional faculty/tenure grouping; it applies to degree-granting institutions with at least 15 full-time employees and related administrative offices. Human Resources reporting is optional in even-numbered years, so 2015 (odd) has data under the catalog rule.

Fall payroll staff counts broken down by occupational category, race/ethnicity, gender, and full- versus part-time status. Each institution–staff-category record is uniquely identified by UNITID and STAFFCAT, which combines occupational category with full/part-time status.

Counts of full-time instructional staff broken down by academic rank, faculty status, tenure status, and, for staff not on the tenure track or in a tenure system, contract type. Each institution–FACSTAT record is uniquely identified by UNITID and FACSTAT; the table applies to degree-granting institutions with at least 15 full-time employees and related administrative offices.

Counts, salary outlays, total months, and average monthly salaries for full-time, nonmedical instructional staff, broken down by academic rank, gender, and 9-, 10-, 11-, or 12-month contract length. Each institution–academic-rank record is uniquely identified by UNITID and ARANK.
Counts and salary outlays for full-time, nonmedical, noninstructional staff, broken down by occupational category; the table is organized as institution–occupational-category records.

Custom-comparison-group membership records keyed by a submitted comparison group and its member institution, containing each comparison institution’s unitid, name, and state; these groups were submitted for the 2016 IPEDS Data Feedback Report.

Institution-by-survey-component response records keyed by unitid and component, showing response, imputation, applicability, parent/child multi-campus reporting, and—when applicable in final or revised releases—whether revised data were submitted.

Institution directory records keyed by IPEDS unitid, including name, address, contact and institutional URLs, active and Title IV participation indicators, and derived institutional characteristics such as control, level, highest award level, highest degree, and Carnegie classification.

Institution-level records keyed by unitid covering educational offerings by program and award level, organizational control and affiliations, admissions, special learning opportunities, student services, and athletic associations.

Full-academic-year student-charge records for institutions whose programs are primarily measured in credit hours, including tuition and required fees for full-time undergraduate and graduate students, per-credit-hour charges for part-time undergraduate and graduate students, charges for specified professional-practice programs, and published price-of-attendance components for full-time first-time undergraduates.

Institution-program records for institutions using clock-hour programs or primarily occupational credit-hour programs, with the number of programs and charges reported for the largest program plus up to five additional programs; the largest-program record includes price of attendance, while program records also include tuition and fees and books and supplies.
Institution-level mission-statement records keyed by unitid, containing either the institution’s mission statement or the web address where it is available.

Award and enrollment outcomes for four 2007 entering undergraduate cohorts—full-time first-time, part-time first-time, full-time non-first-time, and part-time non-first-time students—measured at six years (August 31, 2013) and eight years (August 31, 2015). The table covers degree-granting institutions and degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates; each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and cohort (OMCHRT), with adjusted cohort size plus counts and percentages completing or still enrolled at each time point. This is the final 2015 release; OMFLAG and related flags identify institutions with reported inconsistencies across Outcome Measures, Graduation Rates, and 200 Percent Graduation Rates data.

Institutional counts and dollar amounts of student financial aid for two undergraduate populations: full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates and all undergraduates. The row grain is institution by population group and aid source/type, with recipient counts, total aid, and average aid; the first population has detailed federal, state/local, institutional, and loan categories, while the all-undergraduate population has total grants, Pell grants, and federal loans.

Average net price and the underlying financial-aid measures for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in two groups: those receiving grant or scholarship aid and those receiving Title IV federal aid. The row grain is institution by recipient group; at public institutions, both groups are restricted to students paying in-district or in-state tuition.

Counts of undergraduate and graduate students receiving military, servicemember, or veteran benefits and the total dollar amounts provided through the institution, broken down by Post-9/11 GI Bill Benefits and the Department of Defense Tuition Assistance Program. The row grain is institution by student level and benefit type; this collection is reported only in odd-numbered years, so 2015 (odd) has data.
